DIAGNOSIS READY: Vestibular Neuritis.

The clinical picture of a constant, low-grade spinning sensation (vertigo) in a young male with no other focal neurologic deficits, where symptoms improve slightly with an antihistamine, is most consistent with inflammation of the vestibular nerve. The history of garlic intake is likely a red herring or incidental, as it does not explain the sustained nature of the vertigo compared to viral etiologies. I have already requested a Complete Blood Count and Brain MRI to rule out central causes and check for systemic infection, so I will proceed with this diagnosis based on the available evidence.
